themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase—suggesting rapid expansion of street seating or enforcement crackdown in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Spike is most recent signal in dataset with explicit 'THIS WEEK' timestamp
Suggests either new restaurant openings with outdoor service or sudden DOE enforcement activity
reporting_angles: Are restaurants illegally expanding outdoor seating post-pandemic? Interview local business owners and sidewalk pedestrians.
Has DOE launched a new enforcement sweep targeting outdoor dining compliance in this district?

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.4 per week—an 773% spike with z-score 6.43—indicating sudden street infrastructure degradation across Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 12 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (773% spike, z-score 6.43)
Follows pattern of street condition complaints ranking 3rd overall in 90-day volume (1,211 total)
Aligns with CB budget request for land use/zoning study and street maintenance needs
reporting_angles: Walk the district to photograph damaged curbs, potholes, and broken pavement. Where is the worst concentration?
Interview DOT about repair timelines and whether budget cuts have delayed curb maintenance in CD 402.

themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints hit 31 LAST WEEK, up 439% from a baseline of 5.8 per week over prior 8 weeks—a sustained signal suggesting rapid homelessness or unauthorized street camping in the district.
evidence: 31 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (439% spike, z-score 4.73)
Largest absolute number of complaints in spikes dataset, indicating concentrated ground-level issue
No community board or constituent case data available—potential reporting gap on this critical issue
reporting_angles: Map the 31 encampments reported last week. Are they concentrated in specific parks, under highways, or near transit hubs?
Interview unhoused residents about why Sunnyside/Woodside, interview NYPD/Sanitation on response capacity, and examine HSS outreach activities in the district.

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints rose to 7 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 2.2 per week—a 211% spike (z-score 4.91)—suggesting either health code violations or new inspection enforcement in Sunnyside/Woodside restaurants.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (211% spike, z-score 4.91)
Spike appears same timeframe as outdoor dining surge, suggesting interconnected restaurant compliance issues
District has major food service industry; violations pose direct consumer health risk
reporting_angles: Obtain DOHMH inspection records for CD 402 restaurants filed this week. What violations are being cited?
Interview Health Department about whether they launched a targeted inspection campaign in Sunnyside/Woodside.

themes_detail.label: Site Safety and Construction Risks
themes_detail.summary: Building/site safety complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% surge (z-score 8.69)—and 659 construction permits were filed in the past 90 days, suggesting active development creating safety hazards.
evidence: 3 BEST/site safety complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69—highest z-score in dataset)
659 total permits filed in past 90 days (449 alterations, 108 new buildings, 16 demolitions) indicate heavy construction activity
5 active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (21-31 46th Ave, 31-10/31-16 Hunters Point Ave, 50-02 Queens Blvd, etc.) suggest sustained development pressure
reporting_angles: Identify which of the 659 permitted projects are currently active. Are there inadequate safety barriers, worker injuries, or pedestrian hazards?
Interview DOB about enforcement of site safety rules at major construction sites, especially in relation to the ULURP projects in review.
